species.season: April 1 – December 15; no recreational crabbing on Wednesdays (except handlines, dip nets, private-property pots, holiday weeks)
species.size: Male hard crab 5 inches Apr 1–Jul 14, 5¼ inches Jul 15–Dec 15; male peeler 3¼ in then 3½ in; soft crab 3½ inches
species.limit: Unlicensed: 2 dozen male hard crabs per person (1 dozen peelers/soft); licensed: 1 bushel or 6 dozen; boat limits 2–4 dozen unlicensed, 1 bushel licensed
species.quote: Minimum Size Limits (measured from tip to tip of spikes) — Male hard crab: April 1–July 14—5 inches. July 15–Dec. 15—5¼ inches. Male peeler crab: April 1–July 14—3¼ inches. July 15–Dec. 15—3½ inches. Soft crab: April 1–Dec. 15—3½ inches. It is Illegal for a Recreational Crabber: To possess an egg-bearing (sponge) crab or any female hard or peeler crab. Unlicensed Individual: 2 dozen male hard crabs; Licensed Individual: 1 bushel or 6 dozen if using a container other than a bushel basket.
species.notes: Recreational crabbers may not keep any female crab in Maryland Chesapeake waters. Hours: ½ hour before/after sunrise to sunset (5 p.m. in the Bay mainstem).

species.zone: Atlantic Ocean, Coastal Bays and tributaries
species.quote: Season April 1–Dec. 31. Hard crabs—5 inches. Soft crabs—3½ inches. Peeler crabs April 1–July 14—3¼ inches, July 15–Dec. 31—3½ inches. Mature female crabs—no minimum size. The taking of sponge crabs is prohibited. One bushel per person if using a bushel basket, 6 dozen if using a container other than a bushel basket; two bushels per boat.

species.season: October 1, 2026 – March 31, 2027; Monday through Saturday, sunrise to noon
species.quote: Season: October 1, 2026–March 31, 2027. Catch Limit: 100 oysters/person/day. Days Allowed: Monday through Saturday. Catch Times: Sunrise–Noon. Minimum Size: Three inches measured from hinge to bill along the longest part of the shell.
species.notes: Maryland residents only. $10 resident oyster license (or free waterfront landowner registration) required. Rakes, diving, hand or shaft tongs only; not from sanctuaries, leases or closed areas.

species.quote: Hard Clams — 250 clams/person/day. Limited to hand-operated gear only, including hand rakes. Minimum Size Limits: One inch transverse measurement. No license required for recreational clam harvest.
species.notes: Maryland residents only, except nonresidents may harvest clams in Worcester County.
